answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps each autonomous agent to an identity vertex anchored by cryptographic stake burning. Creating new identities imposes superlinear cost scaling: an attacker must permanently burn rare reserve assets like jade tokens, where fee schedules carve deep karst erosion into capital reserves. Staking costs scale as $O(n^2)$ for $n$ identities, imposing prohibitive economic friction against mass spoofing.
